Hi Elena — thanks for the data and the clear ask. We ran a quick pass on your export and sketched two practical options that align to procurement timing: 1) Immediate buffered slab + staged top-up, 2) Short-term burst credits + reserved tranche at renewal. High level:

Option A — Buffered slab (Recommended)
- Add a dedicated slab of 60 H100-equivalent slots today as a buffer (hot-standby + autoscale to 90% util target)
- Staged add of +30 slots at the start of Oct and +30 in mid-Nov if uplift continues
- Estimated provisioning ETA: 7–10 business days for initial slab; subsequent increments ~3–5 days if planned
- Cost delta: ~+27% vs current committed rate (we used your median token burn to model)

Option B — Burst credits + reserved tranche (Faster procurement overhead)
- 3 months of burst credits sized to cover projected peak (good stopgap, lower upfront admin)
- Reserved tranche (40 slots) added at renewal to lock a lower committed rate

I've attached a model (buffered_slab_model_v3.xlsx) that shows the cost curves and utilization assumptions. For SLAs: we can offer the Dedicated SLOs on the reserved tranche; the buffered slab will carry a standard provisioning lead-time exception if you need <7 days. That can be handled with a signed short SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preference for Option A or B by Friday 7/28
2) If A, Connor will confirm scheduling and provide a provisioning runbook and tentative start dates.
3) We'll send an SOW stub for procurement to review (I can include an SLA exception for the initial slab if required).

Would you like a quick 30-min session tomorrow to walk the workbook together?

Cheers,
